text:
alex_support: Hey team, getting 503s from our hosted API when it tries to hit internal service `ingest.prod.internal`. Started ~08:12 UTC after a planned Route53 change. Error is either NXDOMAIN or TCP timeout depending on host. Can someone help triage?

sre_oncall: Are these from the Dedicated pool or Private deployment?

alex_support: Private (VPC) customers only. Quick repro: from a customer app host inside VPC: `curl -v https://ingest.prod.internal/health` -> hangs then `upstream connect error or disconnect`. `dig ingest.prod.internal +short @10.0.0.2` -> (no output)

dave_eng: Any DNS changes rolled back? We did a Route53 migration last night but thought it only touched staging.

alex_support: Customer says they didn't change anything. Internal infra team ran a script to consolidate private hosted zones across accounts.

netops: Can you paste `dig +trace` from the app host and the resolver logs? Also what resolver IP are you hitting?

alex_support: Sure, from inside host: ```
> dig +short @10.0.0.2 ingest.prod.internal

# no answer
```

linda_platform: I see a TTL flip in the Route53 change log: ingest.prod.internal had TTL 300 -> 30 -> 300 across accounts. Could be propagation + split-horizon issue where the same zone name exists in two accounts and the VPC assoc changed.

sre_oncall: If split-horizon: one account's private hosted zone covers the VPC now but has no records for `ingest` causing NXDOMAIN. Another account had the records. We should check VPC associations for private hosted zones. @netops can you run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones`+assoc in both prod accounts?

netops: Running quick check, found two private hosted zones with the same zone name `prod.internal` in account A (old) and account B (consolidated). VPC was recently associated to account A's zone which lacks the `ingest` A/ALIAS. Account B had the records. That matches NXDOMAIN.

dave_eng: Ok that explains the NXDOMAIN. Why 503s sometimes?

alex_support: Some app nodes still had cached records via local resolver or DNS cache so they hit the right endpoint, others got NXDOMAIN and fell back to different upstream causing 503 cascade. Also some requests timeout because client tries to hit IP that isn't assigned.

sre_oncall: Next steps: 1) Re-associate the VPC to the hosted zone that contains records (account B) OR export records and create the missing records in account A. 2) Clear resolver caches where possible (restart dnsmasq on jump hosts, TTL expiry). 3) Rollback the VPC association change if immediate fix needed.

netops: I'm preparing the fix. To reduce blast radius, I'll create the missing records in account A (quick) and then we plan to migrate VPC assoc back to B during maintenance. Patch command: ```
# example
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZA123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"ingest.prod.internal","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.10.5.12"}]}}]}'
```

deploy-bot: Notifying affected customers: automated incident alert queued.

aws-ops-bot: Route53: Hosted zone ZA123 (account A) was updated (UPSERT) for ingest.prod.internal at 2026-03-17T08:45:22Z.

dave_eng: Once records upserted, we should monitor queries and 5xx rate. Can someone run `dig +short` from a handful of customer VPC hosts to confirm?

alex_support: Confirmed after upsert: `dig @10.0.0.2 ingest.prod.internal +short` -> `10.10.5.12`. App health checks returning 200 again. Incident impact: ~12 customers, mostly short-lived errors and increased latencies.

sre_oncall: Follow-up: schedule a proper hosted zone consolidation runbook that covers VPC association order, record exports, and TTL strategy to avoid TTL-flip split-horizon. Also add an alert when two private hosted zones share the same name across accounts.

linda_platform: I'll draft the runbook and a script to detect duplicate zone names across org accounts.

alex_support: Thanks everyone. Closing the high-priority escalation, will open a postmortem with timeline. :white_check_mark:
